content: The following references provide a comprehensive overview of research and policy analysis related to alcohol consumption, taxation, and its broader societal and economic impacts: 1. A RAND Europe technical report (TR-412-EC) prepared for the European Commission evaluates the economic impacts of EU alcohol policies, offering insights into their effectiveness and implications. 2. 3. Huang CD (2003) developed econometric models to study alcohol demand in the United Kingdom, commissioned by HM Customs and Excise. 4. The International Alliance for Responsible Drinking (IARD) (2016) reviewed global taxation policies on alcoholic beverages, emphasizing their role in public health and economic regulation. 5. Jacobs et al. (2000) explored the supply-side effects of tobacco control policies, contributing to the broader understanding of substance control in developing countries, as published by Oxford University Press for the World Bank and WHO. 6. Jansen and Keck (2004) examined the intersection of national environmental policies and multilateral trade rules in a working paper by the World Trade Organization. 7. Jarman H (2012) analyzed the interaction between trade law and public health evidence, using the WTO's stance on clove cigarettes as a case study, published in Tobacco Control. 8. Jernigan D (2000) applied commodity chain analysis to study changes in alcohol supply in developing countries, with findings published in Addiction. 9. Johnson et al. (1992) investigated shortand long-term elasticities of alcohol consumption in Canada using an error-correction mechanism, published in The Review of Economics and Statistics. 10. Jones SRH (2003) examined brand-building and structural changes in the Scotch whisky industry since 1975, as detailed in Business History. 11. Junor et al. (2004) assessed the macroeconomic and distributional effects of reduced smoking prevalence in New South Wales, published by the Cancer Council of New South Wales. 12. Kahneman D (2003) provided a psychological perspective on bounded rationality in behavioral economics, published in the American Economic Review. 13. 14. Karrenbrock JD (1990) analyzed the globalization of the beer brewing industry, published in the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis Review. 15. Kehoe et al. (2012) evaluated population-level alcohol consumption models and their impact on estimating alcohol-attributable harms, published in Population Health Metrics. 16. Keen M (1998) explored the balance between specific and ad valorem taxation in Fiscal Studies. 17. Kesselman and Cheung (2004) analyzed tax incidence, progressivity, and inequality in Canada, published in the Canadian Tax Journal. 18. Klingemann H (2001) highlighted the social consequences of alcohol consumption in a report by the WHO Regional Office for Europe. 19. Koricheva and Gurevitch (2013) discussed the role of meta-analysis in research synthesis, as outlined in the Handbook of Meta-Analysis in Ecology and Evolution. 20. Lachenmeier et al. (2007) reviewed the knowledge and future directions regarding surrogate alcohol, published in Alcoholism: Clinical and Experimental Research. 21. Lachenmeier DW (2009) addressed the harm reduction potential of addressing unrecorded alcohol products in The Lancet. 22. Lachenmeier and Rehm (2010) examined the impact of the German alcohol monopoly on public health and consumer safety, published in Sucht. 23. Lachenmeier et al. (2011) discussed policy options for addressing unrecorded alcohol in the International Journal of Drug Policy. 24. Lachenmeier et al. (2013) contributed to a comprehensive book on alcohol science, policy, and public health, published by Oxford University Press. 25. Laslett et al. (2011) surveyed the range and magnitude of alcohol's harm to others in Australia, published in Addiction. 26. Lim et al. (2012) conducted a comparative risk assessment of disease burden attributable to 67 risk factors, including alcohol, published in The Lancet. 27. Mäkelä and Österberg (2009) reviewed the effects of alcohol tax cuts in Finland in 2004, published in Addiction. 28. Mamudu et al. (2011) analyzed the conflict between international trade and public health during the FCTC negotiations, published in Tobacco Control. 29. Mazzocchi M (2006) applied the EM algorithm to study time patterns in UK alcohol and tobacco demand, published in Computational Statistics & Data Analysis. 30. Medina-Mora et al. (2000) contributed to a WHO publication on drinking patterns in developing countries. 31. Meier et al. (2009) emphasized the importance of modeling population heterogeneity in alcohol price regulation, published in Addiction. 32. Moffatt M (2012, 2013) provided accessible explanations of economic concepts such as short-run vs. long-run dynamics and cross-price elasticity of demand. 33. Muchlinski P (1996) analyzed competition in the Czech beer industry during economic transitions, published in the Modern Law Review. 34. Myles GD (1996) discussed optimal taxation in imperfect competition, published in International Tax and Public Finance. 35. The National Institute for Health and Welfare (2012) published a statistical yearbook on alcohol and drug statistics in Finland. 36. Nelson JP (2013, 2015) conducted meta-analyses on alcohol price and income elasticities and binge drinking, published in Health Economics Review. 37. The New Zealand Law Commission (2010) released a report on reducing alcohol-related harm. 38. Nordlund and Österberg (2000) examined unrecorded alcohol consumption in Nordic countries, published in Addiction. 39. The OECD (2012) reported on consumption tax trends. 40. Rabinovich et al. (2009) analyzed the affordability of alcohol in the EU, prepared for the European Commission by RAND Corporation. 41. Ranson et al. (2002) discussed the public health implications of multilateral trade agreements in a Cambridge University Press publication. 42. Rehm et al. (2004, 2009, 2010a, 2010b, 2014) contributed extensively to the understanding of alcohol use, its global burden, and unrecorded consumption, with publications in The Lancet, Addiction, and Population Health Metrics. 43. Rerchupan S (2005) reviewed international experiences in alcohol taxation in Asia. 44. Room et al. (1998, 2000, 2001, 2002) explored alcohol's role in economic development, violence, and public health, with publications in Addiction and the Journal of Substance Use. 45. Salo M (1990) analyzed off-premise alcohol sales in Finland. 46. Saspin et al. (2003) discussed international trade and public health advocacy in the Journal of Law, Medicine & Ethics. 47. Selvanathan and Selvanathan (2005) examined the demand for alcohol, tobacco, and marijuana globally. 48. Shaffer et al. (2005) addressed global trade and public health in the American Journal of Public Health. 49. Shield et al. 50. Slama K (2006) advocated for earmarked taxes for health promotion in Promotion and Education. 51. Smith GS and Barss P (1991) highlighted the neglected issue of unintentional injuries in developing countries, published in Epidemiologic Reviews. 52. Smith S (2005) discussed economic issues in alcohol taxation in a book on excise taxation by Oxford University Press. 53. Sornpaisarn et al. (2010, 2012a, 2012b, 2013, 2014, 2015a, 2015b, 2016) extensively studied alcohol taxation policies in Thailand and their implications for public health, with publications in Addiction, Alcohol and Alcoholism, and the Journal of Public Health. 54. Stockwell et al. (2012, 2013) evaluated the impact of minimum alcohol pricing in Canada, published in Addiction and the American Journal of Public Health. 55. Sundström and Ekström (1962) analyzed beverage consumption in Sweden. 56. Svensson J (2009) studied alcohol imports and consumption patterns in Sweden, published in Nordic Studies on Alcohol and Drugs. 57. The United States Census Bureau (2005) released an economic census report. 58. Vathesatogkit et al. (2013) discussed sustainable financing for health promotion in Thailand. 59. Vihmo J (2006) analyzed price elasticities of alcohol in Finland. 60. Vingilis et al. (1998) examined the compatibility of trade agreements with alcohol control policies. 61. Wagenaar et al. (2009b, 2010) conducted meta-analyses on the effects of alcohol pricing and taxation on consumption, morbidity, and mortality, published in Addiction and the American Journal of Public Health. 62. Warner KE (2000) addressed myths and realities in the economics of tobacco in Tobacco Control. 63. Willis J (2003) explored the boundaries of criminal enterprise in Kenya's alcohol industry, published in African Affairs. 64. Wittwer and Anderson (2002) analyzed the impact of tax reforms on Australia's wine industry, published in Australian Economic Papers. 65. The World Health Organization (2002, 2010a, 2010b, 2011, 2012, 2014) published reports on global alcohol and health strategies, tobacco tax administration, and non-communicable disease prevention. 66. Zhang et al. (2002) evaluated the employment impact of tobacco control policies for the World Bank. 67. Ziegler D (2006, 2009) assessed the challenges posed by international trade agreements to alcohol and tobacco control policies, published in Drug and Alcohol Review and Addiction.
